problem: Long-horizon mobile pick-and-place built by sequentially chaining separately trained skills (e.g., STRIPS/LLM planners over learned nav/pick/place, as in Habitat 2.0 TP-SRL, SayCan, TidyBot) fails at hand-offs. For example, navigation stops the robot where picking or placing is impossible, and the fixed sequence cannot recover from disturbances. Monolithic end-to-end RL needs heavily tuned rewards. Classical TAMP needs pre-built maps, precise object locations or teleoperation.
motivation: Assistive tidying robots must run in unseen, large, cluttered homes with only onboard sensing and must survive hardware glitches, moved objects and dynamic obstacles. The authors observe that most failures of modular pipelines are hand-off errors at skill boundaries and out-of-distribution states the isolated skills never saw. A monolithic policy trained with a sparse long-horizon reward cannot learn the task at all.
key_idea: Keep a library of frozen RL-trained visuomotor skills (nav, pick, place). Train on the full task with a sparse reward: (i) a hierarchical mixture-of-experts gating policy that decides from observations which skills are active, and (ii) a corrective policy whose actions fill the action sub-spaces left unselected. Warm-start the gate with DAgger from a sequential-skill teacher.
insight: Replacing a fixed skill sequence with an observation-driven coordinator removes most hand-off errors: Seq-skills → ASC-NoCorrective gives about +12.6% averaged over the Apartment, Lab and simulation columns. A separate corrective policy handles states that are out-of-distribution for the skills, such as approaching a receptacle closely, which the collision-averse nav skill refuses to do; it adds about +6.4% more. Fine-tuning the skills instead causes catastrophic forgetting (43.9% vs 94.9% in sim). A monolithic policy fails (35.8%) even with DAgger warm-start. Without DAgger pre-training of the gate, sparse-reward RL collapses to 5.6%. Recurrence helps mainly when navigation goals are farther from the pick/place targets (hard set: GRU 65.4 vs MLP 60.73). ASC is insensitive to the reward weights (92.8–94.87).
method: Navigation skill π_nav: PointNav-style RL policy trained on 800 HM3D scenes. Inputs: concatenated front depth (240×212), egomotion pose and goal (x,y,θ). Outputs: base velocity v∈[-0.5,0.5] m/s, ω∈[-30,30]°/s. Success is within 0.3 m / 5°. Dense geodesic-plus-heading reward with collision and backward penalties.

Pick skill π_pick: arm policy on gripper depth (240×228), a binary bbox mask of the target from an object detector, and arm joints. Outputs joint deltas that search for the object and center it at 0.3–0.75 m. It then triggers the Boston Dynamics grasp API on the bbox-center pixel once the angle stays below 15° for 4 steps. Trained in ReplicaCAD with YCB clutter/distractors; the object is kinematically attached in sim.

Place skill π_place: blind policy (arm joints plus target xyz) outputting joint deltas. The reward encourages reaching within 0.1 m of the target and pointing the gripper downward within 0.4 m before release.

Skill coordination π^coord: hierarchical mixture-of-experts gating network π^z. Tanh outputs are thresholded to binary z_i. Skills with complementary action spaces (base vs arm) can be co-active; among skills sharing an action space only the arg-max is active. a_coord = Σ z_i a_i.

Skill correction π^corr: a policy trained on the full task that outputs base+arm actions, used only for action sub-spaces where no skill is selected. Final action a_ASC = a_coord + a_adapt. Coordination and corrective policies reuse the frozen visual encoders of the nav and pick skills and see the superset of observations.

Training: all policies are trained with DD-PPO in Habitat-Sim using approximate kinematic Spot simulation. The gate is pre-trained with DAgger (1.3M steps) using the Seq-skills logic as teacher. Gate and corrective policy are then jointly fine-tuned with a sparse task reward (10·success − collision/backward/action-magnitude penalties − 0.01 slack) for 150M steps. Nav skill: 190M steps; pick/place: 18M steps.

Sim-to-real: the policy runs at 2 Hz on a laptop GPU (~5 ms inference). Low-level control uses the BD velocity, arm and grasp APIs with BD odometry for egomotion; BD base obstacle avoidance is off, so all collision avoidance is learned. Real depth is denoised with fast depth completion. The target detector is Mask R-CNN trained on 100k synthetic COCO composites (Owl-ViT for in-the-wild demos).

setting.backbone: Small CNN (3 conv) + 2-layer MLP + GRU policies (nav, pick, place skills; MoE gating coordination policy; corrective policy), trained from scratch with DD-PPO / DAgger; Mask R-CNN (ResNet-101 FPN) detector for target bbox
setting.training_data: Simulation only (Habitat-Sim). Navigation: 800 HM3D scans, 190M steps. Pick/place: 104 ReplicaCAD layouts with 13 YCB objects on 4 receptacle types, 18M steps. Coordination/corrective: DAgger 1.3M steps, then RL 150M steps on ReplicaCAD rearrangement episodes. Detector: 100k auto-labeled images made by pasting U2-Net-segmented object contours onto COCO backgrounds. No real-world robot data.
setting.observation: Two front depth images (concatenated), gripper depth, target bounding-box mask (detector on gripper RGB), arm joint angles, egomotion (BD odometry) relative to start, approximate receptacle pose goal (x,y,θ) and place target (x,y,z)
setting.action_space: Continuous base velocity (v∈[-0.5,0.5] m/s, ω∈[-30,30]°/s) plus arm joint-position deltas (up to 10° per step) at 2 Hz; grasping executed by Boston Dynamics grasp API given a pixel
setting.simulator: Habitat (Habitat-Sim; HM3D + ReplicaCAD), approximate kinematic simulation; deployed on real Boston Dynamics Spot
setting.privileged: Approximate receptacle poses given (sim: sampled from GT object/place locations; real: recorded by teleoperating to each receptacle); place target location (x,y,z) given; egomotion from BD odometry. No map, obstacle layout or precise object location. The Seq-skills-premapping baseline uses a pre-built BD GraphNav map.

numbers_note: Results are task success rates only. There are no standard navigation benchmarks; all evaluations are custom real-world (Spot) and ReplicaCAD simulation mobile pick-and-place. Text and table differ slightly on some baselines' standard errors (ASC-NoCorrective-Finetune 43.9 ±1.3 in the table vs ±1.2 in the text; ASC-NoDAgger 5.6 ±0.6 in the table vs ±1.0 in the text). Other own ablations in sim, not listed as separate entries: ASC-NoCorrective-Finetune 43.9, ASC-NoDAgger 5.6. Reward-weight sensitivity: 92.8 / 93.5 vs 94.87. Robustness to object displacement: 9/9 grasps for <±0.3 m offsets, 3/6 for ±0.6 m. Qualitative deployment in 6 more real environments is reported only in figures/videos.
results: On a real Spot deployed zero-shot from simulation, ASC rearranged 59/60 objects: 96.7% in a 185 m² apartment and 100% in a 65 m² lab. Seq-skills reached 76.7%/70.0% overall 44/60, and Seq-skills-premapping, which uses a pre-built BD GraphNav map, reached 73.3%/70.0%. Both baselines failed mainly from hand-off errors. In simulation over 1500 ReplicaCAD episodes, ASC reaches 94.9% vs 92.3% without the corrective policy, 87.8% Seq-skills, 43.9% skill fine-tuning, 35.8% Mono-RL and 5.6% without DAgger. The learned skills also succeed where the stock BD API fails: obstructed and cross-room navigation 100% vs 0%, occluded picking 18/18 vs 6/18.
limitations: Limited to pick-and-place of small objects from open receptacles with only three skills. Approximate receptacle poses must be provided (recorded by teleoperation in the real world), and goals are not specified in natural language.

Relies on Boston Dynamics proprietary low-level controllers, odometry and the grasp API; the place skill is blind. Sim uses kinematic approximation (object kinematically attached), so contact-rich manipulation is not learned.
Quantitative real-world evaluation is small: 60 episodes in 2 environments, in static single-agent settings. Large object-position perturbations are handled only 3/6 times.
